name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

prose.intro_html:
Here is the kind of dinner I love to find. You cube raw chicken, blend a creamy sauce in about a minute, and dump everything into one 9x13 dish. No boiling the pasta first, no browning the meat, no pile of pots in the sink. The oven does the work while you go live your life.

The math is what closes the deal. You are looking at {{protein}} grams of protein a serving for {{cal}} calories, and every bit of it comes out of one casserole dish at about ${{cost_ps}} a plate. That is a high-protein dinner punching well above its price, and it starts with 5 minutes of prep.
prose.shop_smart:
The sauce is the whole trick, and it leans on two dairy items: cottage cheese and Boursin. Reach for full-fat cottage cheese if you can, since it blends smoother and thicker and gives the sauce its body. The Boursin Garlic and Fine Herbs comes in 5.2 ounce packages, and this batch runs through a little over two of them, so pick up three and you will have a nub left for toast.

On the artichokes, buy canned hearts, not the marinated jarred kind that fights the lemon. You are draining down to a pound and a quarter of hearts, which works out to roughly two and a third cans depending on the brand. Frozen peas are the move over fresh here, since they go straight in from the freezer with no prep and no waste. And grate your own parmesan off a block if you have five minutes; it melts smoother than the pre-grated tubs and you control how much lands on top.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 400 degrees and lightly grease a 9x13 dish. Everything happens in that one pan, so set it where you can reach it.

Build the sauce first. In a blender or food processor, drop in the cottage cheese, Boursin, garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Blend until it is dead smooth, then pour in the chicken broth and blend again. It is going to look alarmingly thin. That is exactly right. The dry pasta drinks it up in the oven.

Now dump and layer. Spread the dry penne across the bottom, then scatter the raw chicken cubes, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the sauce over the whole thing and press the pasta down so every noodle is submerged. Anything sticking out will bake into a crouton.

Cover the dish tight with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it, peel off the foil, and give it a real stir. The pasta should still be a touch underdone at this point. Top with the parmesan and slide it back in for another 5 to 10 minutes, and you can nudge the temperature up if you want the top golden. If the pasta already feels done, just add the parmesan and skip the extra bake.

Let it rest at least 10 minutes before you dig in. It firms up as it sits and the sauce sets. Finish with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
prose.portion_html:
This one is built for 14 servings, and portioning is where you lock in the macros. The honest way is to weigh it. Set an empty container on the scale, zero it out, then weigh the full casserole dish before you dish anything up. Take that cooked weight, divide by 14, and that number is your grams per container.

Scoop to that number, not by eye. Casseroles settle unevenly and the chicken and artichokes love to clump, so eyeballing it means one box is a protein jackpot and the next is sauce and noodles. Fourteen even containers is how you actually hit {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories a serving, every day of the week.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters. One 9x13 dish turns into 14 dinners, and each one lands around ${{cost_ps}}. That is a full plate with {{protein}} grams of protein, not a sad little diet lunch you are hungry an hour after.

Stack that against a drive-through combo or a grocery-store rotisserie meal and it is not a close call. You are eating better food for a fraction of the money, and the only work you put in was 5 minutes of prep and letting the oven run.

head.description: A no-boil dump-and-bake chicken pasta casserole with artichokes and peas. One 9x13 dish makes 14 high-protein, budget-friendly meal-prep dinners with a creamy cottage cheese and Boursin sauce.
head.keywords: no-boil chicken pasta casserole, dump and bake casserole, chicken artichoke pasta, high protein meal prep, budget casserole, cottage cheese pasta sauce, chicken penne bake
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease a 9x13 casserole dish.

In a blender or food processor, blend the cottage cheese, Boursin, garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt until smooth, then add the chicken broth and blend again until the sauce is thin and completely smooth.

Spread the dry penne across the bottom of the dish, scatter the cubed raw chicken, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts on top, then pour the sauce over everything and press the pasta down until it is submerged.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then remove the foil and stir well, leaving the pasta slightly underdone.
Top with the parmesan and bake uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the heat if needed, until the top is golden.
Rest at least 10 minutes, garnish with chopped parsley or basil, and serve.
